tasks.content:
Complete the '## Technical Notes' section of the existing sprint file at apps/flashcards/docs/how/sprints/sprint-3-solege-theme/sprint.md.

Context to read first:
- apps/flashcards/docs/how/architecture.md — full architecture including RenderEngine, ScoreEngine, ScoreAudioEngine, VexFlow, Tone.js sections
- apps/flashcards/docs/how/adr-001-vexflow-svg-rendering.md — VexFlow decision
- apps/flashcards/docs/how/adr-002-tonejs-audio-playback.md — Tone.js decision
- apps/flashcards/docs/what/epics/epic-3-solege-theme/epic.md
- apps/flashcards/docs/what/epics/epic-3-solege-theme/user-stories/us-011-score-engine.md
- apps/flashcards/docs/what/epics/epic-3-solege-theme/user-stories/us-012-score-audio-engine.md
- apps/flashcards/docs/what/epics/epic-3-solege-theme/user-stories/us-013-solege-dataset.md
- apps/flashcards/docs/what/epics/epic-3-solege-theme/user-stories/us-014-solege-theme-picker.md

The Technical Notes section must cover:
1. Architecture decisions with references to ADR-001 (VexFlow) and ADR-002 (Tone.js)
2. Implementation guidance for ScoreEngine:
   - VexFlow 4.x API: how to create a Renderer with SVG backend, a Stave, a Voice, and render notes
   - ScoreData interface and note/duration mapping
   - How to clear and re-inject SVG into the target HTMLElement
3. Implementation guidance for ScoreAudioEngine:
   - How precompute() pre-schedules Tone.js sequence (use Tone.Part or Tone.Sequence)
   - Why render() triggers Tone.Transport.start() — the flip IS the user gesture
   - Idempotency: stop and reset Transport before re-scheduling
   - AudioContext start: call Tone.start() inside render() to unlock AudioContext
4. Engine registration in main.tsx (score and score-audio IDs)
5. Dataset structure for solfege.json (21 cards, 7 notes × 3 durations)
6. Bilingual note display: how the card front shows 'do / C', 'ré / D', etc.
7. Notes on existing tests — no changes to other test files
8. Related architecture links

Preserve all existing content in the sprint.md file (frontmatter, H1, description, Cross-references section). Only fill in the '## Technical Notes' section — replace the placeholder comment with real content.
